claim: LLM ideas are rated more novel than expert human ideas by blind expert reviewers before any execution (novelty 5.64 vs 4.84; rerank 5.81; N=49 per condition, 79 reviewers); feasibility and overall are not better.
agent_test: Blind review of our agent's ideas vs a plain-model baseline at equal tokens; score novelty and feasibility separately.

claim: The novelty advantage disappears after execution: executed AI ideas lose 1.05 novelty, 1.76 excitement and 1.88 effectiveness points while human ideas stay flat (N=43 executors, ~103 h each). Pre-execution judging is a poor guide. Appendix check: ideation-to-execution correlations are near zero for AI ideas (overall Pearson -0.09, excitement -0.32; N=43 total).
agent_test: Run each candidate idea to a measured result in code before selection; compare rank by judge vs rank by outcome.

claim: Independent reviews disagree about as much as LLM judges do (human balanced agreement 56.1%; best LLM ranker 53.3%); LLM-as-judge of ideas is near chance for fine ranking, so a model must not be the final selector.
agent_test: Compare model-judge pick vs code-run pick on the same candidate pool at equal tokens.

claim: Brute-force idea generation saturates: of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 5% (~200) are non-duplicates at cosine 0.8. More samples from one model add little diversity.
agent_test: Measure unique-candidate count vs samples for our S3; test whether fresh-context plus operator prompts raise unique count at equal tokens.

claim: Symbolic regression with LLM proposals plus a numeric evaluator beats classical search at far lower evaluation count (LLM-SR 2.5K iterations vs 2M+ for baselines; out-of-domain NMSE ~0.0037 on E. coli vs >1 for others).
agent_test: Propose-evaluate-feedback loop with code scoring on held-out points vs plain sampling at equal tokens.

claim: LLM equation discovery is inflated by memorisation: on textbook Feynman forms results are low-error in under 20 iterations, but on transformed or synthetic problems the best system gets only 31.5% (LSR-Transform) and 28.1% (LSR-Synth) symbolic accuracy.
agent_test: Evaluate our agent only on mutated or unseen problems; report the gap between original and transformed versions.

claim: Non-LLM structure-exploiting search already solves the textbook set (AI Feynman 100/100 vs Eureqa 71; bonus 90% vs 15%) but is brittle on noise and real-world data (SRBench: 53% exact at zero noise, beaten by four methods above noise 0.01). SRBench numbers: AI Feynman 53% exact recovery at zero noise vs 27% next best; above noise 0.01 four methods beat it. LLM-based SR noise fragility not yet tested.
agent_test: Test O3 decompose and O6 change-representation on noisy tasks; check gain survives noise.

claim: Evolutionary program search with an LLM and a code evaluator finds verifiable new results: AlphaEvolve matched best known on 75% and beat state of the art on 20% of 50+ open problems; 4x4 complex matmul in 48 multiplications; kissing number d=11 raised to 593. FunSearch: cap set 512 in n=8 found in only 4 of 140 runs; bin packing beat best fit on all seven test sets (e.g. Weibull 100k excess 0.03% vs 3.79%) using about 10^6 samples.
agent_test: Evolve candidates with an exact scorer in code; compare to best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: Agentic data-driven discovery benchmarks remain low: DiscoveryBench best 25%, ScienceAgentBench 32.4% (34.3% with expert knowledge), MLE-bench bronze+ 16.9% pass@1 and 34.1% pass@8, PaperBench 21.0%.
agent_test: Allocate tokens by difficulty on a subset of these tasks; compare with uniform allocation.

claim: More inference compute helps agents: o1-preview 42.2% vs 32.4% on ScienceAgentBench (>10x cost); pass@8 doubles pass@1 on MLE-bench; AI co-scientist Elo rises with time without saturation. Gains are uneven: PaperBench o1 plateaus after about 1 h while humans overtake after 24 h. Counter-evidence: PaperBench o1 plateaus after about 1 hour and humans overtake after 24 h.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of one long run vs several short fresh-context runs on a discovery task.

claim: Fully automated paper pipelines fail often in independent tests: 42% of experiments crash (5 of 12), poor citations (median 5; 5 of 34 recent), wrongly judged novelty; DeepReviewer rated all 28 papers from 5 systems as reject.
agent_test: Require code-verified outputs and a novelty search step; count claims that fail re-run.

claim: AI-written papers can pass a low bar: one of three AI Scientist-v2 manuscripts scored 6.33 at an ICLR workshop (about top 45%); the other two were rejected; the Jr. AI Scientist was rejected at Agents4Science.
agent_test: Not directly testable on our agent; use only as an external calibration of reviewer bar.

claim: LLM reviewers are no better than humans and unstable: AI Scientist reviewer 65% vs 66% balanced accuracy, correlation 0.18 vs 0.14 between humans, yet rejected 9 of 10 OpenReview papers in an independent test, including 4 humans accepted. Larger test: ReviewerToo on 1,963 ICLR 2025 papers: ensemble LLM 81.8% accept/reject accuracy vs 83.9% human average, single prompt about 70%; reviewers drift positive after rebuttal.
agent_test: Check judge calibration against held-out outcomes before using any judge in selection.

claim: Unattributed idea overlap is common: experts judged 24.0% of 50 LLM research proposals to be verified plagiarism (scores 4 and 5); automated tools (Turnitin, OpenScholar) caught 0%.
agent_test: Add retrieval-based novelty check (search for source) in S4 and measure rate of flagged ideas.

claim: A multi-step autonomous scientist produces mostly accurate reports but weak synthesis: Kosmos 79.4% of 102 statements accurate (data analysis 85.5%, literature 82.1%, synthesis 57.9%).
agent_test: Audit final-claim statements by type (computed, cited, interpreted) and verify only the interpretive ones.

claim: Co-scientist-style generate-debate-rank tournaments produce experimentally supported hypotheses (3 of 5 AML drugs reduced viability in vitro), but the ranking is by LLM Elo, and top systems o3-mini-high and R1 were competitive at much lower compute.
agent_test: Compare tournament selection vs plain voting vs code scoring at equal tokens.

claim: Sharing prior results among agents raises benchmark scores modestly: AgentRxiv 11.4% relative gain on MATH-500 from prior research, 13.7% with multiple labs; 3.3% average transfer. The +11.4% is a single-agent result (one lab reading its own papers) and the best method was chosen on the same MATH-500 test set; transfer gain is +3.3%.
agent_test: Test a retained-notes memory across tasks vs none at equal tokens.

claim: FunSearch needed about 10^6 LLM samples and 150 CPU evaluators; its headline n=8 cap set (512) appeared in 4 of 140 runs (about 3%), while full admissible sets I(12,7) appeared in 60% of runs. Verified-scorer search finds new results but hit rate per run is low and compute is large.
agent_test: Report hit rate across repeated runs, not best run; log samples per success.

claim: Idea-stage judge scores do not predict executed outcome for AI-generated ideas (Pearson overall -0.09, excitement -0.32 over executed ideas, N=43), and overall judged value after execution tracks effectiveness (r=0.654).
agent_test: Compute rank correlation between pre-run judge score and run outcome on our own candidates.

claim: LLM reviewer ensembles approach human accuracy on accept/reject (81.8% vs 83.9% on 1,963 ICLR 2025 papers) but single reviewers are about 70%, extreme personas are biased, and reviewers turn more positive after rebuttal.
agent_test: Use opposed-persona ensemble as screen; hide rebuttals from critic.

claim: Agent time-vs-score curves flatten early: o1 plateaus after about 1 hour on PaperBench while humans keep improving and overtake after 24 h (41.4% vs 26.6% on a 3-paper subset).
agent_test: Plot score vs token budget for scaffold and plain loop; check where each plateaus.

claim: No source found runs generate-test-select against best-of-N at equal tokens for discovery. Closest (Nova, 100 ideas per method; 5-architecture study with 30 ratings) match idea counts, not compute.
agent_test: Run the control ourselves: same token budget, plain sampling plus code-run selection vs scaffold.

claim: Classical robot scientists have few reproducible quantitative rates in sources opened: Eve screened about 14,400 compounds at over 10,000 per day with a three-loop active-learning selection of 96 per loop; Adam's 12 of 20 hypotheses confirmed is only a secondary report. Not comparable with LLM benchmarks.
agent_test: none; use only as context.
